change.summary: Before each permission scenario, reset the worker Office workspace while preserving its required workflows. This clears claimed runs left by earlier Office runtime-token E2E setup.

ci.test: Office taskless routine permissions › rejects the request when the launched profile does not auto-approve
ci.first_attempt: failed after 180000 ms; Expected finished, Received queued
ci.retry: passed; retry summary classifies this test flaky (attempt statuses failed, passed)

actual_root_evidence.worker_order: On CI worker 0, agentctl-cli tests ran first. At least the first eight seed claimed runs for runtime-token setup, then the permission test ran on that same worker/backend. The suite has no e2eReset in those API-only tests.
actual_root_evidence.mechanism: MaxConcurrentInstance defaults to 8. evalInstanceCeilingGate counts every runs row with status='claimed' (WHERE 1=1). The office test harness seeds claimed rows, and their direct run rows have no workspace_id. Eight such rows fill the instance claim pool, so the taskless routine run remains queued and never reaches the permission handler. The CI failure is test-fixture state contamination, not a permission delivery failure.
actual_root_evidence.local_red: With the first eight claim-seeding agentctl-cli tests followed by the failing permission case, local retries=0 reproduced the exact 180-second failure and queued status. Four predecessors passed because they did not fill the eight-run ceiling.
actual_root_evidence.ci_artifacts: The failed error-context records queued. The trace bundled beside it is from the successful retry and was not used as failed-attempt proof. The exact shard log has no Office permission/scheduler lifecycle events; its backend dump contains unrelated integration-cleanup and generic filesystem warnings.
